raw_response:
My land is about 5 mu. I've farmed this same plot since I was a young woman. My mother farmed it before me. Everyone in our village grows winter wheat and summer corn — that's what this land is for, that's what the soil knows, and that's what the grain buyers come to collect. I wouldn't grow cotton or vegetables. I don't know how to sell them, and I can't afford a bad year.

For the wheat, I plant in October after the corn is off. I buy the seed from the village shop — the same improved variety I've used for several years. It does well. I put down the compound fertilizer at sowing, then spread urea in the spring when the wheat starts to green up. I irrigate before sowing if the soil is dry, again before winter sets in, and once more at jointing. Three times is usually enough. I spray for weeds in early spring and once more if aphids get bad before harvest.

For the corn, I seed it right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I don't turn the soil; I just open a furrow and drop the seed in. The summer rains help a lot, so I only need to water once or twice if it's a dry year. I put urea down when the corn is knee-high. I spray herbicide early and watch for corn borer.

I don't experiment. I do what works. My expected yields are modest but reliable.
